text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament approves the 1997 budget with a 53-15 majority vote in favour, Prime Minister Kabariti says the government seeks to set up a savings fund for employees to help finance housing. Kabariti also stresses self-sufficiency and growth to eliminate poverty and unemployment.
- Transport Minister issues details of instructions on transporting goods between Jordan and Israel along border crossings
- Start of release of second batch of detainees covered under the royal pardon.
- Police confiscate $805,200 forged dollars printed by a person with an Arab nationality while trying to pass them in the local market.
- Head of the Jordanian follow-up committee of the U.N. compensation fund for Gulf War victims hopeful funds will arrive soon for some claimants.
- Religious Affairs Minister arrives in Saudi Arabia on Sunday to discuss affairs of Jordanian pilgrims during the coming Haj (Moslem pilgrimage) season.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says during the debate on the 1997 budget "the Jordanian ambition is bigger than any government and this is secret of our progress."
- Kabariti says will take measures to prevent rise of monopolies in the privatisation stage of the public sector.
- Health Ministry rejects large quantities of food products imported for Ramadan (the Moslem fasting month) which do not conform to Jordanian specifications, say food importers.
- The government plans to take the views of the private sector in formulating the draft anti-monoploy law, officials say.
- Kabariti to address business and industry leaders on Sunday on "challenges facing Jordan as it moves to the 21st century."
- Kabariti tells parliament that development oriented reforms will be balanced by measures to address their impact on the poor.
- Transport arrangements between Jordan and Israel that will ease problems faced by exporters to the Israeli market to take effect on January 1.
- British Minister of State at the Foreign Office with special responsibilities for the Middle East, Jeremy Hanley, is due to arrive in Amman on January 6 in his first official visit.
